also: I’m so happy to see you
I’m so glad to see you
I haven’t seen you for ages

terms.comment: Said by the one who waits; to a woman salvam, to several salvōs vōs.

phrases.latin: Mea māter, salvē. — Gaudeō vēnisse salvum.
phrases.english: Mother, hello. — I’m glad you’ve come back safe (the son arriving, the mother waiting)

phrases.latin: Ō pater, pater mī, salvē. — Salvē multum, gnāte mī.
phrases.english: Father, my father, hello! — A hearty hello, my son.
You’ve come! O happy news for me!
Hello, my son, how I have longed for you!
I’m so glad you’ve come safe.

phrases.latin: Ō mī gnāte, quam libenter tē videō!
phrases.english: Oh my boy, I’m so happy to see you!

phrases.latin: Ō Theopropidēs, ere, salvē, salvom tē advēnisse gaudeō. Ūsquin' valuistī? — Ūsque ut vidēs. — Factum optimē.
phrases.english: Oh, Theopropides, master, hello! I’m glad you’re back safe. Have you been well all this time? — All the time, as you see. — Excellent.

phrases.latin: sīc salūtās atque appellās, quasi dūdum nōn vīderis
phrases.english: you greet me and speak to me as if you hadn’t seen me for ages

phrases.latin: Ō, quam diū tē nōn vīdī! Ūsquin' valuistī?
phrases.english: Oh, long time no see! Have you been well all this time?

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 405.
